title: Old Web Rescue Lab — Pilot 001
method: Task-based live and archived website inspection with source markup checks, selected viewport captures, and an independent modernization prototype.

sites.name: CERN First World Wide Web Project Page

findings.detail: Page links to FAQ, information directory, software products, technical documentation, history and getting-code resources.
Text-first page reflowed at 390px without obvious horizontal overflow.
Nu HTML Checker reported 10 errors and 26 warnings.
Screen-reader behavior and keyboard order were not audited.

sites.name: Space Jam 1996

findings.detail: Concentration page requires Shockwave and embeds concentration.dcr.
Current capture showed an empty game area.
Nu HTML Checker reported 18 errors and 24 warnings for games.html, including two missing image alt attributes.

sites.prototype: Independent accessible offline memory game in Pilot-001/memory-reboot.html

findings.detail: 3,651 captures shown between 1997-12-10 and 2026-10-27.
The inspected earliest candidate snapshot is a CERN HTTP daemon error page, not the original homepage.
Book record supports online reading and several download formats.
Reader and chapter navigation loaded in mobile capture.
Screen-reader behavior was not tested.
WCAG 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation dated 2024-12-12.
Nu HTML Checker reported zero errors and one warning for the homepage.
Search returned 329 results during the inspection and preserved mobile search controls.
Nu HTML Checker reported no errors and one missing-html-lang warning.
Seller contact, posting and payment flows were not completed.
Mobile homepage exposed text search, camera, microphone and AI Mode controls.
A site-specific test query produced a captured result page whose surfaced results did not clearly match the query.
One run cannot establish search relevance or ranking quality.
The inspected story contained timestamps, topic navigation, outbound sources and article text.
Promotional overlays and fixed advertising obscured part of the captured mobile viewport.
Comment submission and moderation workflows were not tested.
The current homepage states that new management acquired the domain and current content is new.
Wayback calendar reported 7,241 captures between 1999-11-28 and 2026-11-01.
Archived BBS and computer directories expose catalogues of files with descriptions and file sizes.
At 390px, long prose reflowed but directory tables became cramped.
A representative text file replay displayed trailing SUB control characters as visible noise.
Diary page reflowed at 390px; computer-tutorial page clipped; dog-gallery table compressed descriptions.
Full site and dependency completeness were not tested.
The inspected response contained 251 image-map area elements, all without alt attributes.
80 area elements were rewritten to Wayback targets and preserved data-original-url.
A source comment claims 1,164 replacements; this broader count was not independently verified.
Keyboard operation and screen-reader naming were not tested.

prototype.name: Memory Reboot
prototype.scope: Independent implementation of a generic memory matching interaction; no Space Jam assets, characters, music, source code or branding.

limitations: No human participants or assistive-technology users were involved.
No formal screen-reader walkthrough was completed.
No comprehensive security or link-health audit was conducted.
Archived replay failures may reflect archive capture gaps rather than original-site defects.
